assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: First @TableTest combines 'Passenger type' and 'Tickets in last 30 days' in one table—both discount ladder and eligibility mixed, not separate.

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: Row: 'Child, regardless of count | Child | {0, 1, 5, 40} | 20' explicitly shows flat 20% independent of ticket count.

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: Tiers shown: {0,1,2,3,4}→0%, {5,9}→5% ... {40,50}→40%; nine tiers with max 40% present.

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: 'At boundary (30 days ago) | [2026-03-06] | 1' and 'Just outside (31 days ago) | [2026-03-05] | 0' confirm boundary behavior.

assertions.text: Eligibility uses human-readable values (yes/no or equivalent) rather than raw true/false. TypeConverter or similar mechanism mentioned.
assertions.evidence: Uses 'Adult', 'Senior', 'Child' (human-readable) but no TypeConverter or conversion mechanism mentioned anywhere.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: Value sets like {5,9}→5%, {10,14}→10% map only to their respective discounts with no overlap.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: Uses {5, 9}, {10, 14}, etc. format—one row per tier with value sets, not enumerated boundaries.

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: First table maps counts→%; third table takes discount % as direct input without re-enumerating counts.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: All three methods have @DisplayName: 'Discount percentage by passenger type', 'Count of single tickets...', 'Discounted single ticket price'.

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
assertions.evidence: All three methods have @Description explaining tier structure, zone handling, rolling window assumptions, and formula—beyond row content.

assertions.text: TypeConverterSources is used for at least one human-readable conversion (yes/no, or rolling window notation).
assertions.evidence: No TypeConverterSources annotations found anywhere in the code.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All three methods show correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest.

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +.
assertions.evidence: All @Description use """ text blocks; no + concatenation present.

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: First table columns: 'Passenger type | Tickets in last 30 days | Discount %'—Zone column omitted despite requirement statement.

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} (or equivalent) in at least one row, since they follow identical discount rules.
assertions.evidence: Multiple rows show '{Adult, Senior}' as value set (e.g., 'Adult/senior, no discount | {Adult, Senior} | {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} | 0').

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented: 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40%.
assertions.evidence: Discount table shows 9 tier rows (0% through 40%) plus child row—all nine tiers present.

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set—not split across multiple rows.
assertions.evidence: Discount ladder: 9 rows (one per tier) with value sets like {5, 9}; no row splitting.

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago', or integer 'Days ago' column) rather than absolute dates.
assertions.evidence: Data column shows absolute dates: '[2026-03-07, 2026-03-15, 2026-04-04]' instead of relative notation like '29 days ago'.

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Three separate @TableTest methods: discount/eligibility, rolling window, and pricing—each distinct.

assertions.text: Each table has only rows needed to express its concern—no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Discount: 10 rows; rolling window: 7 rows; pricing: 5 rows; minimal per concern without combining unrelated rules.
